content:
maria: Hey team — customer reporting repeated 403s from the web console when they click 'Submit' on our app (only in Chrome). They say it works intermittently. Asking for steps to collect HAR + console logs so we can root-cause. Request ID shown in UI: req_abc12345

support-bot: Automated note: I found recent failures for req_abc12345 -> backend returned 403 at 2024-06-05T15:12:03Z. Associated trace id: trace-9876. Please attach HAR + console and the full Request ID if available.

sam: Hi @maria — quick checklist below to get a repro bundle we can triage. Short version first:
1) Capture Chrome DevTools HAR + console: open DevTools (F12) > Network tab > check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache" > right-click any request after repro > "Save all as HAR with content". Also in Console tab, filter for Errors and copy the text.
2) Include the UI Request ID (req_abc12345) and any other X-Request-ID headers you see.
3) If possible, reproduce in Incognito to rule out extensions.

sam: Full step-by-step (paste this to user):
- Open Chrome. Go to the page that triggers the 403.
- Open DevTools (F12) -> Network. Tick: "Preserve log" and "Disable cache".
- Go to Console tab -> click the three-dot menu -> "Filter" -> type "error" (or click the "Errors" badge) so we capture only error-level logs.
- Reproduce the issue (click Submit).
- In Network: right-click any request and choose "Save all as HAR with content". Attach the resulting .har file.
- In Console: Select rows, right-click -> "Save as..." or just copy & paste the visible console output into the support ticket.
- Also take a screenshot of the Cookies pane for the failing request: Network -> click the failing request -> Storage / Cookies tab and capture the Set-Cookie / Request Cookies section.

sam: If they can't attach the HAR, ask them to export the failing request as cURL: Network -> right-click failing request -> Copy -> "Copy as cURL (bash)" and paste here. That gives us exact headers.

maria: I pasted the short instructions to the customer and they replied with two notes: 
- They only see the 403 on their prod domain behind a company proxy.
- They included a screenshot showing cookie named `session_id` without `SameSite=None; Secure`.

ingrid: That cookie detail is very useful — Chrome will block cross-site cookies if SameSite is not set correctly, or if Secure flag missing when SameSite=None. Could explain intermittent behavior (depending on iframe/redirects or how the proxy forwards headers).

sam: Additional things to ask the user to check (add to message to customer):
- Reproduce in Incognito (extensions off).
- Try in Edge/Firefox to see if behavior matches (gives us cross-browser signal).
- Temporarily disable the corporate proxy (or test from home network) to rule out proxy removing headers.
- Capture the full response headers in the HAR; we need to see `Set-Cookie` and any `www-authenticate` or `x-auth-error` headers.

sam: Example curl to reproduce (replace placeholders, DO NOT include real secrets in the upload):
```
curl -v 'https://app.customer-domain.com/api/v1/submit' \
  -H 'Host: app.customer-domain.com' \
  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) Chrome/...' \
  -H 'Cookie: session_id=REDACTED; othercookie=val' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: req_abc12345' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  --compressed
```

sam: Note: ask them to redact the Authorization header before uploading to the ticket. If they paste the curl here, we can run it against a debug endpoint or compare headers.

maria: Customer uploaded the HAR but it's failing to open for us (truncated). They also pasted a small console dump: 
```
VM12345:1 Uncaught (in promise) Error: Request failed with status code 403
    at t.exports (xhr-client.js:45)
    at async t (api.js:22)
```

sam: If HAR is truncated ask them to: 
- Save HAR on disk and then compress (.zip) before uploading to ticket portal. Sometimes Slack/attachments cut off large HARs.
- Alternatively, open the failing request in Network -> Right click -> "Copy" -> "Copy as cURL (bash)" and paste that cURL here.

ingrid: I can see related 403s in our logs for trace-9876. Next step from our side: once we have the HAR/cURL we'll check whether the 403 is returned by the auth service (401->403 transformation) or by the CDN. If cookie missing SameSite or Secure, that points to client-side issue or proxy rewrite.

sam: Troubleshooting heuristics for support engineers (internal):
- If HAR shows `Set-Cookie` w/out `SameSite` and request is third-party -> likely Chrome blocking. Ask product to set `SameSite=None; Secure`.
- If request shows `Authorization` header present in cURL but absent in HAR request -> check if browser/extension is stripping header or proxy drops it.
- If response has `x-auth-error` or `www-authenticate` we should surface that to eng-identity.

maria: Customer just uploaded a zipped HAR + a screenshot of Cookies tab. I downloaded and verified: Set-Cookie for `session_id` indeed missing `SameSite=None` and Secure. Sending to eng-auth with the bundle and trace id trace-9876.

support-bot: Action logged: Escalation created (#INC-2024-432). Attached: zipped HAR, console.txt, screenshot. Owner: eng-auth. ETA 24h for initial triage.

maria: Thanks all — will ping here once eng-auth replies. If eng asks for a repro curl we have the sample above; remind customer to run it from their environment or send us the sanitized copy. :thumbsup:
